newsitem.title: USA: Multicanal sees Q2 improving over Q1.
newsitem.headline: Multicanal sees Q2 improving over Q1.

text.p: Multicanal Holdings SA said Wednesday it expected its second quarter results to reflect "a small improvement" over its first quarter results.
Multicanal, the largest cable TV operator in Brazil, reported a net loss of $9.2 million or $0.01 a share on net revenues of $70.9 million for the first quarter ended March 31.
The Rio de Janeiro-based company said it expects to report its second quarter results by mid-August.
It said that it substantially completed the building and activation of its network during the second quarter. The bulk of the activation occurred in June, it said.
It said its results will still be affected by a high "churn rate" and bad debt provision. Churn rate includes cancellations and disconnections due to service stoppages.
To correct this, Multicanal said it has focused selling efforts in cities with higher than average household income levels, it said.
It said these efforts were launched beginning in late March and although improvements have been evident since May, the full impact should occur in the third and fourh quarters of this year.

Multicanal has stakes in 13 cable television systems that serve 13 cities in southeast and central-west Brazail. Its companies include Multicanal Telecommunicacoes, which owns 10 cable systems and in which it holds a 99 percent stake and and Belo Horizonte, which it wholly owns.
